items.back: $f(x)=Σc_{n}(x−a)^{n}$ on $|x−a|<R$.
$E(z)=Σz^{n}/n!$, converging for all $z$. $e^{x}=E(x)$, $\log$ is its inverse on $(0,∞)$.
$C(x)=\mathrm{Re}\,E(ix)$, $S(x)=\mathrm{Im}\,E(ix)$. $π/2$ is the smallest positive zero of $C$.
$f(x)=Σ_{−N}^{N}c_{n}e^{inx}$ with $c_{m}=\dfrac1{2π}∫_{−π}^{π}f(x)e^{−imx}dx$.
$D_{N}(x)=Σ_{−N}^{N}e^{inx}=\dfrac{\sin((N+\frac12)x)}{\sin(x/2)}$, so $s_{N}(f;x)=\dfrac1{2π}∫f(x−t)D_{N}(t)dt$.

items.front: Power series are continuous and differentiable
items.back: If $Σc_{n}x^{n}$ converges for $|x|<R$, it converges uniformly on $[−R+ε,R−ε]$; the sum is continuous and $f'(x)=Σnc_{n}x^{n−1}$ there. So $f$ has derivatives of all orders and $f^{(k)}(0)=k!c_{k}$.
If $Σc_{n}$ converges, then $\lim_{x→1^{−}}Σc_{n}x^{n}=Σc_{n}$.
If $Σ_{i}Σ_{j}|a_{ij}|$ converges, the iterated sums can be taken in either order.
A power series about 0 can be re-expanded about any $a$ inside the interval of convergence.
If two power series agree on a set with a limit point in $(−R,R)$, they have the same coefficients.
$E(z+w)=E(z)E(w)$; $e^{x}$ is increasing and positive; $x^{n}e^{−x}→0$; $\log$ is continuous, increasing, $\log(xy)=\log x+\log y$.
$e^{iz}$ has period $2π$; $e^{it}$ maps $[0,2π)$ one-to-one onto the unit circle.
Every nonconstant complex polynomial has a complex root.
The Fourier partial sum $s_{n}$ minimizes $∫|f−t|^{2}$ over trig polynomials $t$ of degree $n$. $Σ|c_{n}|^{2}≤\dfrac{1}{2π}∫|f|^{2}$, so $c_{n}→0$.
If $|f(x+t)−f(x)|≤M|t|$ for small $|t|$, then $s_{N}(f;x)→f(x)$.
A continuous $2π$-periodic $f$ is a uniform limit of trigonometric polynomials.
For Riemann integrable $2π$-periodic $f$: $\dfrac1{2π}∫|f|^{2}=Σ|c_{n}|^{2}$, and $s_{N}→f$ in the mean-square sense.
$Γ(x+1)=xΓ(x)$; $Γ(n+1)=n!$; $\log Γ$ is convex.
$Γ$ is the only positive function on $(0,∞)$ with $f(x+1)=xf(x)$, $f(1)=1$ and $\log f$ convex.
$B(x,y)=Γ(x)Γ(y)/Γ(x+y)$; $Γ(1/2)=\sqrt π$. $Γ(x+1)\sim(x/e)^{x}\sqrt{2πx}$.

items.modelProof: $E(z)E(w)=Σ_{n}Σ_{k}\dfrac{z^{k}w^{n−k}}{k!(n−k)!}=Σ_{n}\dfrac{(z+w)^{n}}{n!}$. The Cauchy product is justified by Mertens (3.50) since both series converge absolutely.
Integrate $∫_{0}^{∞}t^{x}e^{−t}dt$ by parts: the boundary term vanishes and what's left is $x∫t^{x−1}e^{−t}dt$.

items.prompt: Compute the Fourier series of $f(x)=x$ on $(−π,π)$ and use Parseval to find $Σ1/n^{2}$.

items.modelProof: The alternating series converges (3.43), so Abel's theorem lets $x→1^{−}$: $\log(1+x)→\log 2$.

items.prompt: A power series with radius $R$ converges uniformly on $(−R,R)$.
items.explanation: $Σx^{n}$ on $(−1,1)$. It is uniform on every $[−r,r]$ with $r<R$.

items.prompt: An infinitely differentiable function equals its Taylor series near each point.
The Fourier coefficients of a Riemann integrable function tend to 0.
If two power series agree at $x=1/n$ for every $n$, they are identical.
items.explanation: 0 is a limit point of $\{1/n\}$ inside the interval; identity theorem (8.5).
Abel's theorem needs $Σ(−1)^{n}$ to converge first. It doesn't, so the limit of the power series says nothing about the series at $x=1$.

lines: Power series can be differentiated term by term.
items.explanation: Term-by-term differentiation keeps the radius but can lose endpoints. At $x=1$, $Σ1/n$ diverges. 8.1 only applies to the open interval.

lines: A function with derivatives of every order equals its Taylor series near the point.
items.explanation: Existence of all derivatives doesn't make the Taylor series converge to $f$. Here the series is identically 0 while $f(x)>0$ for $x≠0$.

items.name: $e^{−1/x^{2}}$
items.details: Smooth, not analytic at 0: its Taylor series is 0.

items.name: $Σ(−1)^{n}x^{n}=1/(1+x)$
items.details: The limit as $x→1^{−}$ is $1/2$ but $Σ(−1)^{n}$ diverges. The converse of Abel's theorem fails.

items.name: $Σx^{n}/n$
items.details: Converges at $x=−1$ (to $−\log 2$) but not at $x=1$. Endpoint behavior is independent at each end.

items.name: Square wave $\mathrm{sgn}(x)$ on $(−π,π)$
items.details: Fourier series converges to 0 (the midpoint) at the jump, and overshoots near it (Gibbs phenomenon).
